A day’s drive to the Valley, and the haul bags up to the base of the Nose.
You called in at Coffee Shop: a day's leave, 2 left this year.
Registration and insurance: $72. The week's bills don't care about your card.
The repeaters have had their say on Bot’s Edge: V13, as you called it. It goes in the book at that, and nobody argues.
El Capitan, Yosemite, USA: The Nose. 6 pitches, food and water for 10 days, with Hazel. You lead first. The dog stays with friends at the Lot.
Pitch 1 fixed. 5 to go, and the next is yours too.

You clip in for the night. The ledge creaks; the haul bag swings.
Hazel makes coffee on the hanging stove like it’s any other morning. It isn’t. It’s the best one.
Hazel leads 2 pitches. You jug and haul behind. 2 to go.
You clip in for the night. The ledge creaks; the haul bag swings.
Hazel says she’s never slept well on a ledge and never wanted to be anywhere else.
You wake up already thinking about the next line.

El Capitan: the summit of The Nose, on day 3, with Hazel. The sponsors pay $2400, and you'll be telling this one for years. +2 head.

Scout has picked a spot in the shade with a view of you, and that is not a coincidence.

You say the thing everyone says: the route isn’t dangerous, the route is honest, and if you can’t climb it as it was climbed, climb something else. The old guard buys your beer. The gym crowd thinks you’re a fossil.
Onsight: Alpine Crimps, V9, on go 1.
Hazel does not say much on the drive back. She does not need to. +2 head.
Ten. Nobody at the gym believes you until someone who was there tells them.

Back at the Lot after the long road, Hazel finally tells you the story she has never told anyone: why she stopped competing, and why she stayed in the van after. You had more than earned it. The fire burns down and neither of you gets up.
The magazine that ran your El Cap photos sends $200 and asks for more.
The lines out here have reputations. Now one of them has a story with you in it.
